fields.description_1:
Schipholparkeren has to turn a travel plan into a parking reservation without making visitors search for the practical steps. Travellers arrive with dates, flight timing, luggage and different expectations about valet or comfort parking. Extra car services can be useful, but they should not distract from the main task of choosing a parking option and securing the reservation.

The site therefore needed a booking path that keeps arrival and return details central, explains the available parking choices and shows optional services at the right moment. Mobile use is especially important because many travellers compare or book before a trip. The portfolio problem was to make that journey clear and dependable without claiming shorter waiting times, guaranteed availability or other operational results that were not verified.
fields.description_2:
I structured Schipholparkeren around the reservation sequence a traveller actually follows. Trip dates and the parking choice come first, followed by the details needed to complete a booking and any optional car services that fit the journey. Practical information is placed near the decision it supports, so visitors do not have to move between unrelated pages before understanding what to do.

The design keeps the reservation action visible without turning every section into a sales prompt. On mobile, date fields, parking options and next steps remain easy to scan and tap. The portfolio case now explains a real booking workflow rather than a generic transport website. It also avoids promising availability, transfer times or service outcomes that depend on live operations outside the website itself.

fields.description_1:
Casareno presents renovation work to homeowners who often start with an idea rather than a complete technical brief. A visitor may be considering a bathroom, floor, door, finish or broader renovation and needs to understand how those services relate before asking for advice. Finished projects provide useful context, but a gallery alone does not explain what can be done or how a project moves forward.

The website therefore needed to balance visual inspiration with service information and a route to contact. The case study also had to stay specific to renovation work instead of using broad claims about craftsmanship or quality without evidence. The challenge was to show what Casareno handles, connect examples to services and keep the next step understandable on desktop and mobile.
fields.description_2:
For Casareno, I organised the WordPress site so completed renovation work and service information support each other. Visitors can start with the type of work they are considering, see relevant examples and then read the practical details that help them decide whether to make contact. Bathrooms, floors, doors and finishing work are separated clearly instead of being hidden inside one broad renovation message.

Project imagery is used as context rather than as a substitute for explanation. Contact actions appear after visitors have enough information to describe their plans, and the same order is maintained on smaller screens. The portfolio story reflects how homeowners explore a renovation project: inspiration first where useful, then service fit and a clear conversation, without inventing price, timing or result guarantees.

fields.description_1:
Pastrycompany combines two buying situations that need different information: ordering food online and arranging catering for an event. A customer choosing a product wants options, price and a cart path, while someone planning catering needs context about the service before sending an enquiry. If both routes are mixed, the webshop can become confusing and event clients may browse products that do not answer their questions.

Reviews and offers can support trust, but they should not replace practical information. The project therefore needed a clear split between direct WooCommerce shopping and service-led catering. The portfolio text also had to avoid unsupported claims about freshness, delivery speed or customer satisfaction. The challenge was making both journeys part of one brand without forcing them into the same process.
fields.description_2:
I structured Pastrycompany so product shopping and catering remain connected but follow their own paths. WooCommerce categories, product details and cart actions support customers who are ready to order, while catering pages explain the event service and lead naturally to an enquiry. Offers and reviews appear as supporting information rather than interrupting the main choice.

This keeps the site useful for a quick purchase without making larger event requests feel like another product checkout. On mobile, product cards, cart actions and catering contact routes keep separate priorities, which makes the difference between ordering and enquiring easier to understand. The portfolio case now describes the actual dual-purpose platform and the decisions behind its structure, without inventing delivery, sales or customer-response results that were not measured.

fields.description_1:
Ourwp offers business-address services to entrepreneurs who need to understand more than a postal location before choosing a package. Registration use, post handling, scanning and account access each affect the service, so a visitor needs to compare what is included and what happens after signup. If the website leads with package names without explanation, people can choose based on price before understanding practical differences.

The service also involves business and postal information, which makes clear wording important. The portfolio problem was to turn operational features into an understandable decision path, keep package comparison readable on mobile and avoid implying legal or registration outcomes that depend on the customer's situation. The site needed to move from explanation to signup without hiding important conditions behind marketing language.
fields.description_2:
I organised Ourwp around the questions an entrepreneur needs answered before selecting an address package. The website explains the address service, post handling and scanning first, then connects those details to package choices and the signup route. Account access is treated as part of the ongoing service rather than as a separate feature with no context.

This order helps visitors compare what they receive before committing to a plan. I kept the wording practical and avoided claims about registration acceptance or legal suitability that require case-specific confirmation. On mobile, package cards, included services and signup actions remain easy to compare. The portfolio entry now shows how WordPress supports a recurring business-address service with clear operational steps, instead of presenting it as a generic subscription website.

fields.description_1:
Byderma brings treatments, appointments and product shopping together, creating a navigation problem that a beauty website or webshop does not have. Someone researching a treatment needs different information from a customer who wants to buy skincare, while members may also look for benefits or account options. If these routes compete on every page, visitors lose context and calls to action become unclear.

The website therefore needed to separate treatment discovery, booking and WooCommerce shopping while keeping them connected as one brand. Beauty content can drift into unsupported outcome claims, so the portfolio story must describe structure rather than promise treatment results. The challenge was to help visitors understand whether their next step is learn, book or shop and keep that choice clear on smaller screens.
fields.description_2:
For Byderma, I shaped the WordPress and WooCommerce experience around three distinct actions: explore treatments, book an appointment and shop for products. Treatment pages provide context before a booking action, while product categories and product pages keep the normal shopping path direct. Member information sits alongside the routes where it is relevant instead of becoming a fourth competing journey.

This separation lets the visual brand stay consistent without making every visitor follow the same sequence. On mobile, treatment cards, booking actions and product controls remain clearly grouped, which reduces the chance of mixing service and shopping tasks. The portfolio case now explains the platform through its real combination of beauty services and ecommerce, while avoiding unsupported promises about skin results, conversion improvement or sales performance.
